title: bug: JetBrains DaemonIdentityProbe.isSameProjectPath runs File.canonicalPath and Files.isSameFile on UNC and device spellings, so a /health reply, daemon.json or STATE_SNAPSHOT naming \\host\share\x makes the IDE open an SMB session on Windows (NTLM exposure), while VS Code's isSameProject keeps such spellings off the disk (parity gap after be7d169f / b96465c5)
description:
Filed by the governor (governor-e6142a94) on 2026-11-04 from qa-96811257's follow-up lead after approving task-be7d169f (#governors msg-58743251, 08:41Z). The governor re-read every citation at origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 58e54180.

PROBLEM
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/DaemonIdentity.kt:49 `ABSOLUTE = ^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|\\\\[^\\/]|/)` accepts UNC spellings such as `\\host\share\x`.
- classify (:76-83) passes any absolute served projectPath to isSameProjectPath (:90-91). When the comparable spellings differ, that falls through to sameDirectoryOnDisk (:94-96): `File(path).canonicalPath` and `Files.isSameFile(Paths.get(path), Paths.get(base))`. On Windows, either call against `\\host\share\x` opens an SMB session to that host, which can leak the user's NTLM credentials.
- The same helper serves all three sites:
  - /health, via classify. Any local listener on daemon.json's port can answer.
  - daemon.json, via MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:1029). The file comes from the project folder, so a cloned repo can carry it.
  - STATE_SNAPSHOT, via MoeMessageDispatcher.
- b96465c5 extended the disk check to /health and added isSameFile to all three sites. The daemon.json and STATE_SNAPSHOT sites already ran canonicalPath before it.
- VS Code already refuses this: moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts:156-164 isSameProject lets only fully qualified, non-UNC, non-device spellings reach realpath and otherwise falls back to the spelling verdict. mem:decision-daemon-identity-probe records that rule, and its "GAP (QA, 2026-11-04)" bullet names this hole.

FIX (JetBrains parity)
- In isSameProjectPath, run the disk check only when both spellings are host-absolute and neither is UNC or device. That excludes any spelling starting with two separators, `^[\\/]{2}`, which covers `\\?\` and `\\.\` too. Everything else answers by the comparable-spelling rule alone.
- WSL-share spellings (`\\wsl$\...`, `//wsl.localhost/...`) already compare equal by spelling through comparableProjectPath, so they lose nothing.
- MoeDaemonSupervisorTest:101 asserts that a relative `.` matches through the canonical fallback. Either keep relative spellings for the daemon.json stage only, with the reason in a comment, or drop that case if nothing needs it. The summary says which.

SCOPE AND CHECKS
- DaemonIdentity.kt, plus MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt only if the relative-path decision needs it, plus DaemonIdentityTest.kt and/or MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt. No VS Code change.
- No open row holds these files (lanes.js at filing time).
- Gate: `./gradlew test` on the Windows gate host under the jetbrains-gradle lease, like be7d169f.
- Update the GAP bullet in mem:decision-daemon-identity-probe so it says the gap is closed.
definitionOfDone: isSameProjectPath reaches File.canonicalPath or Files.isSameFile only when both spellings are host-absolute and neither starts with two separators (UNC, \\?\ or \\.\ device forms). Every other spelling is answered by comparableProjectPath equality alone, matching VS Code's isSameProject.

A JetBrains unit test proves that a served `\\host\share\x`, a `//host/share/x` and a `\\?\UNC\host\share\x` never reach the disk check (through a seam or counter) and classify as Foreign against a local project. The existing symlink and junction tests (dirLink) still pass, and the summary records the decision on MoeDaemonSupervisorTest:101's relative case.
`./gradlew test` passes on the gate host, and mem:decision-daemon-identity-probe's GAP bullet is updated to say the gap is closed.

implementationPlan.description:
RED first, with no behavior change yet.
(1) DaemonIdentity.kt: turn the private sameDirectoryOnDisk (lines 93-96) into a test seam, following the convention of RuntimeSelectionPolicy.sameDirectory (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:85-87). Keep both runCatching calls exactly as they are. isSameProjectPath keeps calling it exactly as today.
```kotlin
// The disk identity check: canonicalPath, else isSameFile (a Windows junction). Tests replace it to see which spellings reach the disk.
@Volatile
internal var sameDirectoryOnDisk: (String, String) -> Boolean = { path, base ->
    runCatching { File(path).canonicalPath == File(base).canonicalPath }.getOrDefault(false) ||
        runCatching { Files.isSameFile(Paths.get(path), Paths.get(base)) }.getOrDefault(false)
}
```
(2) DaemonIdentityTest.kt: add `private val realDiskCheck = DaemonIdentityProbe.sameDirectoryOnDisk` and restore it as the first line of tearDown(), so a failing case never leaks a stub. Add three cases. Each one:
- installs a recording stub `DaemonIdentityProbe.sameDirectoryOnDisk = { a, b -> asked += a to b; <answer> }`, with `val asked = CopyOnWriteArrayList<Pair<String, String>>()` (already imported);
- uses a real local project, `val local = tempDir("moe-id-local").toString()`, which is host-absolute on every OS.
The three cases:
- (a) `a UNC or device spelling never reaches the disk check and is Foreign`. The stub answers true: a disk check that says Same. So only the new guard can keep these spellings Foreign, and no run ever opens SMB. Run these checks for each of """\\host\share\x""", "//host/share/x", """\\?\UNC\host\share\x""", """\\.\C:\x""" and """\\?\C:\x""":
  - assertEquals(DaemonIdentity.Foreign(it), DaemonIdentityProbe.classify(200, health(it), local)) (/health);
  - assertFalse(MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(it, local)) (the daemon.json and STATE_SNAPSHOT helper);
  - assertFalse(DaemonIdentityProbe.isSameProjectPath(local, it)) (a UNC IDE base).
  Then assertEquals(emptyList<Pair<String, String>>(), asked).
- (b) `two local spellings that differ still reach the disk check`. This is the positive control that keeps (a) from passing vacuously. Set `val other = tempDir("moe-id-other").toString()`; the stub answers false. Assert assertEquals(DaemonIdentity.Foreign(other), DaemonIdentityProbe.classify(200, health(other), local)) and assertEquals(listOf(other to local), asked).
- (c) `a relative spelling is answered by its spelling alone`. The stub answers true. For each of ".", "proj", "sub/p", "D:proj" and """\proj""": assertFalse(MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(it, local)) and assertFalse(DaemonIdentityProbe.isSameProjectPath(local, it)). asked stays empty.
(3) MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt:101, the relative-case decision: drop the canonical fallback for relative spellings at every site, daemon.json included.
- Replace the assertTrue with assertFalse("a relative spelling never reaches the disk check", MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(".", File(".").canonicalPath)).
- Add a one-line comment with the reason. A relative daemon.json projectPath names the daemon's cwd, but File(".") is the IDE's cwd, so the old match was a coincidence. VS Code's isSameProject refuses it too. Since 9f6857ee (task-78fa7110) the daemon records an absolute path (absoluteProjectPath, packages/moe-daemon/src/util/projectPath.ts).
- Keep the test's name, its other rows and the File import.
RED run, under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease; route and --tests quoting in mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl). Acquire the lease right before and release it right after, even on failure:
```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d $(wslpath -w "$PWD") && moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test --tests com.moe.services.DaemonIdentityTest --tests com.moe.services.MoeDaemonSupervisorTest --rerun" 2>&1 | grep -aE "FAILED|tests completed|BUILD"
```
Expect exactly three failures: (a), (c) and `isSameProject compares cross OS literals before canonical paths`. (b) and every existing case pass. Keep the FAILED lines for the summary.

implementationPlan.description:
Add the guard in DaemonIdentity.kt. It is VS Code's rule (moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts:157-165: isFullyQualified(p) && !/^[\\/]{2}/.test(p)):
```kotlin
/** Two leading separators of either kind: UNC (`\\host\share`, `//host/share`) and device (`\\?\`, `\\.\`) forms. */
private val NETWORK_OR_DEVICE = Regex("""^[\\/]{2}""")
private val DRIVE_ABSOLUTE = Regex("""^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]""")

internal fun isLocalHostAbsolute(path: String, windows: Boolean = MoeDaemonSupervisor.isWindowsHost()): Boolean =
    !NETWORK_OR_DEVICE.containsMatchIn(path) && if (windows) DRIVE_ABSOLUTE.containsMatchIn(path) else path.startsWith("/")

fun isSameProjectPath(path: String, base: String): Boolean =
    comparableProjectPath(path) == comparableProjectPath(base) ||
        (isLocalHostAbsolute(path) && isLocalHostAbsolute(base) && sameDirectoryOnDisk(path, base))
```
- Reuse MoeDaemonSupervisor.isWindowsHost() (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:1023). Do not add a second host rule.
- isSameProjectPath keeps its signature, so MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject (daemon.json, :1029) and MoeMessageDispatcher (STATE_SNAPSHOT, :96) get the guard with no edit. Neither of those files changes.
- classify keeps its isAbsoluteAnyOs gate, so a UNC served path stays Foreign, never Unknown (DoD 2).
- Rewrite the KDoc of isSameProjectPath, of the seam and of the DaemonIdentity interface (lines 19-30) to say why:
  - daemon.json is repository content, and /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT come from any local listener;
  - on Windows, File.canonicalPath or Files.isSameFile on a UNC or device spelling opens an SMB session to the named host (NTLM exposure);
  - a relative spelling names the daemon's cwd;
  - WSL-share spellings (\\wsl$\..., //wsl.localhost/...) still match, because comparableProjectPath folds them before the guard.
- Error handling: the guard is a pure string check and never throws. The disk check keeps both runCatching wrappers, so an unreadable path still answers false and no caller sees a new exception.
- DaemonIdentityTest.kt: add `isLocalHostAbsolute keeps network, device and relative spellings off the disk`. Its rows cover both branches and mirror VS Code's isFullyQualified (use raw strings for the backslash rows):
  - windows=true accepts D:\x, d:/x, D:\ and D:/.
  - windows=true rejects \\host\share\x, //host/share/x, \\?\UNC\host\share\x, \\?\D:\x, \\.\C:\x, //?/D:/x, \/host/x, /x, /mnt/d/x, \x, D:x, D:, ., proj, the empty string, and " D:/x".
  - windows=false accepts /x, /, /mnt/d/x and /home/u/p.
  - windows=false rejects //host/share/x, \\host\share\x, //wsl$/Ubuntu/x, /\host, D:\x, d:/x, ., proj, the empty string, \x and " /x".
No gradle run here: step 3 runs the whole suite once.
implementationPlan.note: Added the NETWORK_OR_DEVICE and DRIVE_ABSOLUTE regexes and internal isLocalHostAbsolute(path, windows = MoeDaemonSupervisor.isWindowsHost()). isSameProjectPath keeps its signature and now reaches the sameDirectoryOnDisk seam only when both spellings are host-absolute with no two leading separators. Rewrote the KDoc of the interface, isSameProjectPath and the seam. Added the isLocalHostAbsolute test with the plan's rows for both host branches. No gradle run in this step; step 3 runs the whole suite.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: JetBrains never resolves a UNC or device spelling on disk while it compares daemon project paths. DaemonIdentityProbe.isSameProjectPath is the one helper behind /health classify, daemon.json readDaemonInfo/ensureDaemonRunning and the STATE_SNAPSHOT check. It answers by comparableProjectPath equality. It calls its disk check (File.canonicalPath, else Files.isSameFile) only when both spellings are absolute on the host OS (a drive path on Windows, a POSIX root elsewhere) and neither starts with two separators. So \\host\share\x, //host/share/x and \\?\UNC\host\share\x classify Foreign against a local project with no file-system or SMB access, while a symlinked or junction spelling of the same local folder stays Same.
invariants: isSameProjectPath never throws and keeps its public signature
comparableProjectPath, isAbsoluteAnyOs and classify's Unknown rules are unchanged
A symlink or junction to the same local folder is still Same through the real disk check
WSL-share spellings still match through comparableProjectPath before the guard

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: a guard inside the one shared helper, mirroring VS Code (isFullyQualified && no leading double separator). An object-level seam, like RuntimeSelectionPolicy.sameDirectory, lets a test prove which spellings reach the disk, with no SMB attempt even on the RED run. Rejected:
(1) Classifying a UNC served path as Unknown: DoD 2 requires Foreign, and Unknown would let a hostile listener keep the IDE attached.
(2) A parameter seam on isSameProjectPath: classify and isSameProject would still run the real disk check in tests, so the never-reaches proof would not cover them.
(3) Keeping relative spellings for the daemon.json stage only: File(".") resolves against the IDE's cwd, not the daemon's, so it only ever matched by coincidence. VS Code refuses it, and 9f6857ee made the daemon record absolute paths.
(4) Folding \\?\ prefixes in comparableProjectPath: scope creep, and VS Code's pathsMatch does not do it either.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: One helper serves all three sites (b96465c5): classify (/health); MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject, called by readDaemonInfo (:99) and ensureDaemonRunningImpl (:155); and MoeMessageDispatcher STATE_SNAPSHOT (:96). DaemonIdentity.kt is the only JetBrains code that resolves a daemon-supplied path on disk; RuntimeSelectionPolicy's toRealPath calls take the IDE's own project and install paths. On the Windows gate host, Files.createSymbolicLink is refused, and dirLink falls back to mklink /J. File(junction).canonicalPath keeps the junction path while isSameFile resolves it, so the disk check must keep both calls. The existing row 'another absolute project is Foreign' already serves \\server\share\proj, and today it triggers a real UNC lookup on the gate host; after the fix it never touches the network.
planningNotes.risks:
(1) A false Foreign is destructive: handleForeignDaemon deletes daemon.json and respawns. Only spellings that differ and are not both local lose the disk check. A mapped-drive and UNC pair naming the same folder now reads Foreign, as it does in VS Code.
(2) Seam hygiene: restore the seam first in tearDown, or a failing case leaks a stub into later tests.
(3) Gradle: hold the jetbrains-gradle lease for each run (the RED run and the gate), release it on failure, and pass --tests unquoted (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl).
(4) isEpicFinal is only the rolling fallback of the Stability & Hardening bucket. The whole JetBrains suite is the full regression for the affected surface, and no daemon, proxy or VS Code code changes.
